state:
**Goal `growth-proof`, Stage 3 is still red; Stage 4's first slice is on disk.** No floor is carried.

`bun nv scaling --iterations --sized` on this tree ends `942 flat, 1 grow, 8 unclear, 440 skipped` and `7 benches run more iterations than their ramp needs`, exit 1, in about 30 minutes. It never passed at the driver after the last lowering. The output this session kept did not name the eight benches. `--budget` passes.

The selection engine has a `bench` atom: `bench:benches/members/.../x.nvs`, listed by `benchFiles`, defined by `benchDef` (the proof files plus the `.scale.nvs` and `.twin.nvs` siblings), and a sibling's edit maps to its bench through `benchOf` (all `tools/nv/select/atoms.ts`). `recordBench` in `tools/nv/proofs/select.ts` records one bench from a run of a copy at its smallest batch; nothing calls it yet. `tools/nv/test/bench-selection.test.ts` pins the three tests the Stage 4 check names.

`discover` (`tools/nv/select/select.ts`) does not list benches yet, on purpose: a bench atom no tool runs would stay selected as `new` in every `nv verify` and sweep. It joins `discover` in the same slice that makes `nv affected --run` run them.

The clock at the lowered N mostly reads 0 (`ns_per_op 0.0`). Whether to time the clock at a larger, clock-only N is the user's call, and nothing has changed for it.

items.text: **Name the eight.** Run `bun nv bg bun nv scaling --iterations --sized` and save the whole output under `.agent-tmp/`, because the list comes before the final summary lines. The verdict is printed at `tools/nv/cmd/scaling.ts:1338`, and `oversized` is at `tools/nv/cmd/scaling.ts:1038`. Spec: `rule:testing/feature-proofs`, the goal's Stage 3.

**Close them.** Lower the seven oversized benches with `--sized --lower`. Judge the bench that grows: either a real cost that grows, which is a gap record or a fix, or a ramp that is too short at its new N. Then run `--sized` again to make sure the lowering is stable. A lowered N whose re-ramp settles one batch higher is the likely cause, and that would mean `oversized` (`tools/nv/cmd/scaling.ts:1038`) needs more slack.
